issues.legal_issue: Mortgagees’ rights are extinguished when a mortgage remains subsisting at the commencement of the law governing separation of evacuees’ interests, even if the claimed period for acquiring ownership expires afterward.
material_facts: The land had been mortgaged with possession, and the claimant alleged that the mortgagees entered into possession in 1892.
On the claimant’s account, the 60-year period would expire in 1952, after the relevant Act came into force in 1951.
The mortgage remained subsisting when the Act came into force, and the successors to the mortgagors had become evacuees.
A mutation-register entry gave the date of the mortgage document, not the date possession began.
issues.conclusion: The mortgage was subsisting when the Act came into force, so Section 9(2) extinguished the mortgagees’ rights before the claimed 60-year period expired. The dismissal of the possession suit was upheld and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 9(2) of the Evacuee’s Interest (Separation) Act, mortgagees’ rights are extinguished where the mortgage is subsisting when the Act comes into force. The claimed 60-year period had not expired by then; the date in the mutation-register entry referred to the mortgage document, not the commencement of possession. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.mortgagor_successors_were_evacuees: The persons who succeeded to the mortgagors had become evacuees.
predicates.mortgage_subsisting_at_commencement: The mortgage remained unredeemed and subsisting when the relevant law took effect.
predicates.redemption_period_unexpired_at_commencem: The period relied on to claim ownership through possession had not expired when the relevant law took effect.

issues.definition: When the mortgagors’ successors are evacuees, the mortgage remains subsisting at the law’s commencement, and the claimed period for acquiring ownership has not yet expired, the mortgagees’ rights are extinguished.
